Read the transcript of the audio guide
  1. Around 1893 a family of Russian Jews fleeing persecution landed in New York with almost nothing. source
  2. Their youngest son, a boy called Israel Baline, would grow up to write "God Bless America." source
  3. Berlin was born Israel Baline on 11 May 1888 in the Russian Empire. source
  4. The exact town is genuinely uncertain. source
  5. His father died while Israel was still a boy, and he left school to help support the family, selling newspapers and singing for coins. source
  6. He became a singing waiter in the saloons of the Bowery, and there began putting his own words to the tunes of the day. source
  7. A printer set his name on the sheet music as "I. Berlin," and he kept it. source
  8. In 1911 "Alexander's Ragtime Band" made him famous on both sides of the Atlantic. source
  9. Berlin took his oath as a United States citizen on 6 February 1918, after several years of paperwork. source
  10. Within months the new citizen was drafted. source
  11. It was around this time, too, that he first drafted a patriotic song he judged too solemn, and put it away in a drawer. source
  12. In 1938, with war returning to Europe, Berlin took that song back out and reworked it. source
  13. The singer Kate Smith introduced "God Bless America" on the radio on 11 November 1938, and Berlin assigned its royalties to a fund for the Boy and Girl Scouts. source
  14. Four years later, in the film Holiday Inn, he introduced "White Christmas," which became one of the best-selling songs ever recorded and won him an Academy Award. source
  15. He said this the same year he brought out "God Bless America": source
  16. I'd like to write a great peace song, but it's hard to do, because you have trouble dramatizing peace. source
  17. Why might someone who arrived as a newcomer write the songs a whole country sings?
